title: Mcp Security Oauth 2 1
motto: Remote MCP servers need authorization, not just authentication. The 2025-11-25 spec aligns with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + resource indicators (RFC 8707) + protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728). SEP-835 adds incremental scope consent with step-up authorization on 403 WWW-Authenticate. This lesson implements the step-up flow as a state machine so you can see every hop.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Remote MCP servers need authorization, not just authentication. The 2025-11-25 spec aligns with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + resource indicators (RFC 8707) + protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728). SEP-835 adds incremental scope consent with step-up authorization on 403 WWW-Authenticate. This lesson implements the step-up flow as a state machine so you can see every hop.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Early MCP (pre-2025) shipped remote servers with ad-hoc API keys or even no auth. The 2025-11-25 spec closes that gap with a full OAuth 2.1 profile.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: OAuth 2.1 secures MCP servers with scoped tokens.

steps.title: Implement oauth
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.

code.starter:
def token_scopes_ok(granted, required):
    return all(s in granted for s in required)
